title: Welcome to the Ningxin Huida Newsroom
author: NXHD Team
excerpt: We are launching a new insights channel — covering fastener engineering, manufacturing quality, and the industries we serve (aerospace, railway, construction, machinery).
content:
We are excited to launch the **Ningxin Huida newsroom** — a place where we share engineering know-how, manufacturing updates, and the stories behind the fasteners that hold critical structures together.

## What you'll find here

- **Engineering deep-dives** — practical guidance on selecting standard, special and self-tapping fasteners for demanding applications.
- **Quality & testing** — notes from our ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 audited processes, including tensile, torque and salt-spray testing.
- **Industry case studies** — how our parts are integrated into railway, aerospace, construction and industrial OEM projects.

## How to get in touch

If you'd like a quote, a technical review of an existing drawing, or a CoC/test report, drop us a message at **[contact@nxhdmfg.com](mailto:contact@nxhdmfg.com)** — typical response time is **under 24 hours**.

We post new articles roughly **once a week**, with longer technical pieces roughly every two weeks. Thanks for reading — and welcome aboard.

title: ISO 9001 / 14001 / 45001 Recertification Successfully Completed
author: Quality Team
excerpt: Our three ISO management systems were re-certified this quarter by an accredited body, covering the Handan and Datong plants. Open the post for the scope statement and the new certificate numbers.
content:
Our three ISO management systems — **ISO 9001:2015 (Quality)**, **ISO 14001:2015 (Environment)** and **ISO 45001:2018 (Occupational H&S)** — were re-certified this quarter following the surveillance audit of both manufacturing plants (Handan, founded 2020, and Datong HQ, founded 2025).

## What the audit covered

- Incoming material inspection for carbon steel, stainless steel and alloy wire/rod
- Heat-treatment, surface-finishing and packaging process control
- Calibration of tensile / torque / hardness testing equipment
- Documented traceability from raw-material batch to finished goods
- Hazard identification for cold-heading, thread-rolling and salt-spray operations

The audit closed with **zero major non-conformities**. Updated certificates have been published to the Quality page — please request the latest PDFs from your account manager if you need them on file for supplier approval.

## What it means for customers

- **Documented material traceability** on every shipment, including batch heat numbers and mechanical test results.
- **Process consistency** validated by external surveillance — useful when your supplier-quality team asks for an audit report.
- **Environment & H&S controls** documented per ISO 14001 / 45001 — required by some EU and APAC OEMs.

title: Self-Tapping Screws in Light-Gauge Steel: Choosing the Right Tip Geometry
author: Engineering
excerpt: Self-drilling vs. self-tapping, thread-forming vs. thread-cutting, and the tip-geometry trade-offs when fastening into 0.6–1.5 mm cold-formed steel.
content:
Choosing the right self-tapping screw for light-gauge steel (0.6 – 1.5 mm) comes down to **three questions**: are you fastening into a pre-punched or pre-drilled hole, or not? Is the substrate uniform or multi-layer? And what holding force do you actually need?

## Quick reference

| Substrate | Tip type | Typical thread | Drive |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.6–0.9 mm steel | Thread-forming (Type A) | Fine, spaced | Phillips / Torx |
| 1.0–1.5 mm steel | Thread-cutting (Type B/T) | Coarser | Torx preferred |
| Steel-to-aluminium | Thread-cutting (Type B) | Coarse | Torx |
| Multi-layer (steel+wood) | Self-drilling tip + thread-rolling | Coarse | Torx / hex |
| Pre-drilled hole | Machine screw thread | Standard M-class | Phillips / hex |

## Why the tip matters

- **Thread-forming (Type A)** displaces material — good for thin, ductile substrates but can cause stress marks around the joint.
- **Thread-cutting (Type B/T)** actually removes chips — cleaner in multi-layer joints, less driving torque.
- **Self-drilling tips** add a drill point — saves a separate operation but requires close tolerance on perpendicularity.

## Specifying correctly for an OEM

If you are designing a new assembly and want predictable torque-out performance:

1. State the **substrate grade and thickness** (e.g. "DC01, 1.0 mm").
2. State the **minimum pull-out and torque-out values** (typically ≥ 1.5 kN for thin steel).
3. Ask for the **washer face diameter** if the joint is on a soft cladding.
4. Specify the **coating** (zinc flake, zinc-electroplated, zinc-nickel, or stainless A2/A4).

Send us your drawing or sample — we will suggest a stock-standard pattern and confirm torque-out data before sampling.
